sentences.text: 2. It is contended on behalf of appellant that the learned writ Court has failed to conduct a proper judicial review under Article 226 of the Constitution of India to assess whether the administrative decision was illegal, irrational, or procedurally improper.

The writ petition was dismissed based on generalized observations rather than addressing the substantive issues, such as the lack of evidence proving that the food served was unhygienic or caused harm to any child.

The reliance on W.A. No.
1477/2019 (Abhishek Swa Sahayata Samooh) was misplaced due to a lack of factual parity with the present case.
The use of disposable plates (Dona/Pattal) was necessitated by water scarcity, not poor food quality.

The learned writ Court ignored NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5875 2 Jai Mata Di Swasahayata Samuh Through ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101553746/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These inconsistencies affect the validity of the action taken.

The learned writ Court further failed to consider the severe civil consequences of the decision,
particularly its impact on the livelihoods of women members of the Self Help Group (SHG).
This omission violates principles of fairness and reasonableness.
Under these circumstances, the appellant prays for setting aside the impugned order.
3. On the other hand, learned Counsel for the State submits that the order of learned writ Court is well-founded, legally sound, and requires no interference by this Court.
The administrative action was justified based on the imperative health and safety concerns regarding the food served to the children.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of this appeal.

4. Having heard the learned Counsel for both parties and after perusing the impugned order along with the available documents, we are of the considered opinion that the findings recorded by the learned Single Judge are based on the facts available on record.
The conclusions drawn are sound and in line with the correct principles of law.
Consequently, no indulgence is warranted in this intra-Court appeal.
5. The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed, being devoid of substance.
No costs.

(ANAND PATHAK) 
 JUDGE   MKB Jai Mata Di Swasahayata Samuh Through ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101553746/
